clusters.label: NLP Definition and Suitability Criteria
clusters.rationale: c14_pro_thinking_001 defines NLP, and c15_pro_thinking_001 lists characteristics that make NLP suitable for problem-solving. Both describe foundational NLP concepts and could be taught together.

clusters.label: Main Applications of NLP
clusters.rationale: c14_pro_thinking_002 lists four main uses of NLP, overlapping with many specific application candidates from c15 (e.g., information retrieval, machine translation, sentiment analysis). These application candidates form a broad group, but for clustering we keep them together as they all represent NLP applications mentioned across sources.

clusters.label: Google Cloud NLP Tools
clusters.rationale: c14_pro_thinking_003, c14_pro_thinking_004, c14_pro_thinking_005, and c14_pro_thinking_006 all describe specific Google Cloud NLP services (API Natural Language, AutoML, Dialogflow, Document AI). They share the context of Google Cloud and may be grouped as tools for NLP tasks.

clusters.label: NLP Challenges Overview
clusters.rationale: c15_pro_thinking_002 through c15_pro_thinking_011 describe various NLP challenges (segmentation, context analysis, semantic extraction, ambiguity, spelling errors, neologisms, figures of speech/abbreviations, coreference, negation/speculation, and limited Portuguese resources). They all represent common difficulties in NLP and are presented in the same source section.

clusters.label: Regular Expressions Fundamentals and Metacharacters
clusters.rationale: c16_pro_thinking_001, c17_pro_thinking_001, and c17_pro_thinking_002 all define regular expressions and introduce the concept of metacharacters. c16_pro_thinking_002 through c16_pro_thinking_005 detail specific metacharacter types (representatives, quantifiers, anchors, alternation/grouping/escape). These form the core syntax of regex.

clusters.label: Regex Implementation in Python
clusters.rationale: c16_pro_thinking_006 and c16_pro_thinking_007 describe methods of the Python 're' module (match, search, findall, split, sub, group). These are practical implementations of regex concepts.

clusters.label: Extracting Patterns with Regex
clusters.rationale: c16_pro_thinking_008, c16_pro_thinking_009, c16_pro_thinking_010, c16_pro_thinking_011, and c17_pro_thinking_008 all demonstrate practical regex extractions (emails, phone numbers, sentences, acronyms, and validation of common formats). They are applied examples of regex.

clusters.label: Regex in JavaScript
clusters.rationale: c17_pro_thinking_007 specifically discusses regex syntax in JavaScript. It is distinct from Python implementations but still regex-related.

clusters.label: Lexical Similarity and Edit Distances
clusters.rationale: c18_pro_thinking_001 defines lexical similarity, c18_pro_thinking_002 and c18_pro_thinking_003 cover minimum edit distance and Levenshtein distance, c18_pro_thinking_005 and c18_pro_thinking_006 describe Jaccard and cosine similarity, c18_pro_thinking_007 and c18_pro_thinking_008 discuss algorithm classification and granularity, c18_pro_thinking_009 lists applications, c19_pro_thinking_001 defines lexical similarity, c19_pro_thinking_003 lists applications of similarity measures, and c20_pro_thinking_005 mentions dimensionality reduction with PCA (related to similarity). These all relate to measuring text similarity.

clusters.label: N-grams and Text Prediction
clusters.rationale: c18_pro_thinking_004 explains n-grams for text prediction. It is a specific technique within lexical models.

clusters.label: Semantic Similarity and WordNet
clusters.rationale: c19_pro_thinking_002 defines semantic similarity, c19_pro_thinking_004 discusses knowledge-based vs. corpus-based, c19_pro_thinking_005 introduces WordNet, c19_pro_thinking_006 and c19_pro_thinking_007 describe Path Similarity and LCS, c19_pro_thinking_008 lists semantic relations, c19_pro_thinking_009 and c19_pro_thinking_010 show NLTK access to WordNet. All are semantic similarity concepts.

clusters.label: scikit-learn Library and ML Tasks
clusters.rationale: c20_pro_thinking_001 introduces scikit-learn, c20_pro_thinking_002 covers classification, c20_pro_thinking_003 covers model selection, c20_pro_thinking_004 covers preprocessing, c20_pro_thinking_006 covers clustering, and c20_pro_thinking_007 covers regression. These are all scikit-learn features.
